title: Graceful degradation playbook for cross-region variant deployments
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Define and implement a reproducible, operator-friendly playbook and runtime components for graceful degradation during model variant rollouts. The scope covers routing decisions for canaries, A/B tests, shadow traffic, automated failovers across regions and capacity tiers, compatibility gating (signature/IO/kv-cache expectations), and an auto-rollback policy tied to measurable SLO regressions and safety signals.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic orchestration: support incremental weight ramps and immediate throttled rollback when canary error-rate or latency breaches thresholds
Shadow traffic plumbing: capture full request + response traces for shadowed models without affecting production latency or cost buckets
Compatibility preflight: runtime rejects variant with mismatched input/output schema or missing KV cache support and surfaces actionable error
Region failover: automatic routing to secondary region within 2 minutes for regional quota exhaustion with tier-aware capacity selection
Tiered capacity fallback: pressure on high-cost dedicated tier triggers downgrade to quantized variant with documented quality delta
Automated rollback policy: configurable signal set (p50/p95 latency, error rate, hallucination score proxy) with cooldown and audit trail
Dashboarding + alerts: per-deployment canary dashboard, canary vs baseline diff metrics, and runbook link in alert payload
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Initial RFC reviewed with runtime, routing, and console leads. Agreed to separate control-plane signals from data-plane probes (Ava).
2025-02-18: Prototype canary weight controller implemented behind feature flag. Basic ramping + abort API working (PR #8134).
2025-02-25: Compatibility prober design completed: static signature check + live probe sampling for KV cache hot-paths (Diego).
2025-03-01: Integrated shadow traffic tracer with observability pipeline; storage TTL for shadow traces set to 7 days to control cost.
2025-03-03: Load-testing with cross-region failover simulator identified 350ms cold-start spike in eu-west-1 when switching to quantized fallback; mitigation options listed below.
review_feedback: PM review (Rohit Patel): prefer early opt-in by tenant to avoid noisy global rollouts; require per-tenant safety thresholds and override hooks.
Design review (Maya Chen): console UX should show a compact degradation ladder and one-click escape to force-rollback with confirmation modal.
SRE review (Lena Fischer): must include circuit-breaker cooldown and a kill-switch that bypasses automatic rollback for incident investigations.
Security review (pending): ensure shadow traces are scrubbed for PII before ingestion when tenant configuration requires it.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged internal canaries (10% of internal tenant traffic) with shadow tracing enabled; run 1 week of stability tests.
Phase 1: Graduated canary for low-risk public tenants (1% traffic) with A/B buckets for quality measurement and automated abort on signal breach.
Phase 2: Broader rollout with region-aware routing rules and tier mappings; monitor cost delta and QoR (quality of results) signals for 72 hours.
Phase 3: Default policy enabled for new deployments; existing deployments require opt-in via deployment config.
compatibility_checks: Static manifest validation: model artifact must declare input schema, tokenization metadata, kv-cache flag, max-context, and quantization profile.
Binary probe: sandboxed dry-run that executes 50 synthetic requests to validate output shape and failure modes.
KV-cache probe: warm-up sequence for KV operations to ensure backward/forward compatibility of cache keys and TTL behavior.
Latency/throughput fingerprint: short microbenchmark to record p50/p95/p99 for chosen region and hardware class.
automated_rollback_policy: Signals considered: error rate (5xx), client-side observed errors, p95 latency delta > 2x baseline, hallucination proxy increase > 5% over baseline, token cost variance > 20%
Decision engine: weighted scoring where severe signals (errors) can trigger immediate abort; milder signals need sustained breach window (5m to 30m configurable).
Cooldowns: after auto-rollback, block auto-rollforward for 30m and create an audit ticket with captured traces.
Escalation: after 3 auto-rollbacks in 24h escalate to on-call pager with runbook link.
observability_signals: Per-variant: request count, success rate, client-error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, token consumption per request
Quality proxies: hallucination-rate proxy (heuristic), answer-length divergence, rerank score distribution for retrieval-augmented examples
Canary-vs-baseline deltas: confidence intervals for latency and quality metrics shown on canary dashboard
Trace anchors: sample traces for failed requests with payload and model responses (shadow traces marked).
test_plan: Unit tests for routing policy compiler and decision engine (edge cases for weight=0, full-eviction, and region-blacklist).
Integration tests: deploy a synthetic variant into staging, run ramp scenarios and validate rollback triggers fire as expected.
Chaos tests: simulate region outage and capacity tier drains to verify fallback ordering and cache rehydration behavior.
E2E: run a small A/B experiment measuring customer-facing latency and quality using production-like traffic samples (with consent).
